title: Step-count list task
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming 2: data structures, files and subprograms
source: Seeded from computing/y10 lesson 8 (Pupil PDF worksheet: step-count list task)
intro: Lesson 8: Lists and arrays: storing and searching many values. To understand how lists store many values under one name and how to loop through them to search and total

questions.q: Write code to find the average of marks = [62, 75, 48, 90].
questions.a: total = 0; for m in marks: total += m; print(total / len(marks)) → 68.75
questions.model: I do: total = sum by looping: 62 + 75 + 48 + 90 = 275. Average = 275 / len(marks) = 275 / 4 = 68.75.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: a list of 8 daily step counts. Write a program that outputs the total, the highest and how many days were over 8,000.
questions.a: Loop with total, highest, and a counter for values > 8000; answers for the given data on the sheet.
questions.model: The teacher writes the loop header and the counter: count = 0; for s in steps: if s > 8000: count = count + 1

questions.q: Extend: change the linear search to print 'Not found' when found is still -1.
questions.a: if found == -1: print('Not found') else: print(found)

questions.q: Stretch: why is linear search slow on a list of a million names?
questions.a: It may check every item: up to a million comparisons.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: A teacher records 15 test marks. Would you rather have 15 variables or one list? Why?
questions.a: One list: easier to store, loop through, sort and search.
